answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring sustained, non-transferable effort rather than a one-time payment. A new identity arrives like a faint ember with no established weight and must prove its unique utility across many epochs. Its record is a single continuous thread of peer-verified work, which a spammer cannot clone; a sybil farm can only launch a costly voyage of disposable accounts that never gain real standing. Only after this history is anchored does a node earn voting power, keeping the economy decentralized rather than ruled by mass-generated identities.
